title: a > comparison against 0 removes null from a nullable int

ground_truth.statement: When comparing null with an integer, PHP converts both operands to bool. Thus null > 0 compares false > false and is false. The input domain is {null} plus {int}, so null never enters the branch and the argument passed there is an int. The runtime control null > -1 is also false, distinguishing this rule from numeric conversion of null to zero.

allowed.reason: Mago warns on every comparison whose operand may be null, whatever the comparison is used for. That is its intended output: crates/analyzer/tests/cases/issue_2434.php in the Mago repository expects exactly `possibly-null-operand` for `if ($x > 0)` with a `?int $x` parameter, which is this line. The warning does not claim the branch can receive null, and Mago correctly reports nothing for the accept_int() call, which is what this case tests.

notes: From the field: `if ($a > 0)` on a nullable int is a common legacy null guard. The null case is a single value, so the runtime check decides it rather than sampling it. Mago's null-operand warning is acknowledged above with the upstream test that documents it as intended (basis: upstream_test).
